pictures.scene: Veronese, Christ among the Doctors — the young Jesus sits high on the marble steps of the temple in a rose tunic and a dark blue cloak, one hand lifted and the other held open in explanation, while the learned men crowd up the stairs below Him with their heavy books on their knees, one in a yellow cloak hunched over his volume and a white-bearded elder at the right leaning across the balustrade to argue back, the women and the onlookers packed in behind under the great grey columns, one day as jesus was teaching the people in the temple courts and proclaiming the gospel, the chief priests and scribes, together with the elders, came up to him, tell us, they said, by what authority are you doing these things, and who gave you this authority, …
pictures.name: pd_veronese_doctors

pictures.scene: Axentowicz, The Feast of Jordan — a whole village stands out on the frozen river in the snow for the blessing of the water, the tall painted banners and the processional crosses carried up above their heads, a man in a long tan sheepskin coat and a black fur cap waiting in the foreground with his hands folded, a white-bearded old man in a red shirt bowing low beside him, and a girl in a flowered headscarf turning round to look back at us out of the press of brown coats, the lit candles held up in the middle of the crowd, i will also ask you a question, jesus replied, tell me, john's baptism, was it from heaven, or from men, …
pictures.name: pd_axentowicz_feast_of_jordan

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, The Conspiracy of Claudius Civilis — men swear a secret oath by night around a long table in a dark hall, the one-eyed chief in a high gold crown sitting at the head with his great sword lifted, the others reaching in to lay their blades across his so that the steel crosses above the lit cloth, a pale long-haired man at the right holding out a dish and the broad back of another leaning in over his chair in the foreground, nothing lit but their faces and the table, they deliberated among themselves and said, if we say, from heaven, he will ask, why did you not believe him, but if we say, from men, all the people will stone us, for they are convinced that john was a prophet, …
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_the_conspiracy_of_claudius_civilis

pictures.scene: Durer, Christ among the Doctors — the young Jesus in a blue-green robe stands pressed in among the teachers with His long fair hair loose on His shoulders, His eyes lowered and His two hands held up in the middle of the panel counting the argument off on His fingers, a toothless old man at the right leaning his wrinkled face right in to answer and spreading his own hands back at Him, another at the left holding an open book up against his chin, and more hands and books crowding in at every edge in the dark, so they answered that they did not know where it was from, and jesus replied, neither will i tell you by what authority i am doing these things, …
pictures.name: pd_durer_doctors

pictures.scene: Van Gogh, The Red Vineyard — a whole vineyard burning red and orange in the late sun, the pickers bent double in their blue smocks all through the rows with their baskets, one woman holding a green parasol over her head as she walks up the slope, another stooping over the vines in a pale blue skirt, the wet track running down through the middle of the field, the yellow sky and the dark blue trees shut off the top of the hill behind them, then he proceeded to tell the people this parable, a man planted a vineyard, rented it out to some tenants, and went away for a long time, at harvest time, he sent a servant to the tenants to collect his share of the fruit of the vineyard, but the tenants beat the servant and sent him away empty-handed, …

pictures.scene: Brouwer, Fighting Peasants — a quarrel outside a country inn has turned ugly, a man in a blue cap and yellow breeches twisting round with his face open in a shout while he drags a long knife out at his hip, a woman in a white headcloth hanging on his arm to hold the blade down, another man in a fur cap shouting over his shoulder, the jugs and the trestle table shoved aside behind them and the villagers scattering up the hill past the church tower, so he sent another servant, but they beat him and treated him shamefully, sending him away empty-handed, then he sent a third, but they wounded him and threw him out, …
pictures.name: pd_brouwer_fighting_peasants

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, Jacob Blessing the Sons of Joseph — the blind old father sits up in bed in a white nightshirt under a heavy red coverlet and lays his hand on the fair head of the younger boy, his son in a great pale turban bending in over him with a grave smile to steady the dying arm, the dark-haired child beside them looking up out of the picture at us, and the mother standing at the right in her brown gown and gold chain watching the inheritance given away, what shall i do, asked the owner of the vineyard, i will send my beloved son, perhaps they will respect him, but when the tenants saw the son, they discussed it among themselves and said, this is the heir, let us kill him, and the inheritance will be ours, …

pictures.scene: Giotto, The Kiss of Judas — the betrayer in a great yellow cloak throws the cloth around Christ and leans in to kiss Him, the two faces almost touching in the middle of the blue, Christ steady and unmoved with His gold halo behind Him, while the armed crowd closes in on every side with clubs and torches and staves lifted up across the sky, a soldier in a scarlet cloak beside them and a man at the right pointing out the arrest, so they threw him out of the vineyard and killed him, what then will the owner of the vineyard do to them, he will come and kill those tenants, and will give the vineyard to others, and when the people heard this, they said, may such a thing never happen, …

pictures.scene: Fouquet, The Building of the Temple — the great carved front of the temple goes up storey by storey in gold and grey stone, the scaffolding and the lifting wheel still standing on the roof with men hauling on the rope, the king leaning out from a little gallery at the left with his hand raised to give the order, and all across the sand at the bottom the masons kneel at their blocks with mallet and chisel and square, squaring the stones one by one and carrying them in, but jesus looked directly at them and said, then what is the meaning of that which is written, the stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone, everyone who falls on this stone will be broken to pieces, but he on whom it falls will be crushed, …

pictures.scene: Van Dyck, The Tribute Money — Christ stands close up against a grey sky in a red robe and a heavy blue-grey cloak with a thin gold halo burning behind His hair, His face turned away from the man questioning Him and His own hand lifted open at the left, while from the right two hands come reaching in over His cloak, one of them holding the little silver coin out flat on the palm for Him to look at, teacher, they inquired, we know that you speak and teach correctly, you show no partiality, but teach the way of god in accordance with the truth, is it lawful for us to pay taxes to caesar or not, …

pictures.scene: Van Reymerswaele, The Tax Collectors — two collectors crowd over one desk in a dim counting room, the first in a blue gown and a huge red fur hat bending right down over the open ledger with spectacles slipping on his nose as he writes the entry out, the second leaning in over his shoulder in a green cap with his face screwed up in a grin, one finger stabbing down at the page while his other hand turns a coin over by the little scale, the loose money lying scattered across the table beside them, but jesus saw through their duplicity and said to them, show me a denarius, whose image and inscription are on it, caesar's, they answered, …

lines.text: One day as Jesus was teaching the people in the temple courts and proclaiming the gospel, the chief priests and scribes, together with the elders, came up to Him.
Tell us, they said, by what authority are You doing these things, and who gave You this authority?
I will also ask you a question, Jesus replied. Tell Me:
John's baptism, was it from heaven, or from men?
They deliberated among themselves and said, If we say, From heaven, He will ask, Why did you not believe him?
But if we say, From men, all the people will stone us, for they are convinced that John was a prophet.
So they answered that they did not know where it was from.
And Jesus replied, Neither will I tell you by what authority I am doing these things.
Then He proceeded to tell the people this parable: A man planted a vineyard, rented it out to some tenants, and went away for a long time.
At harvest time, he sent a servant to the tenants to collect his share of the fruit of the vineyard. But the tenants beat the servant and sent him away empty-handed.
So he sent another servant, but they beat him and treated him shamefully, sending him away empty-handed.
Then he sent a third, but they wounded him and threw him out.
What shall I do? asked the owner of the vineyard. I will send my beloved son. Perhaps they will respect him.
But when the tenants saw the son, they discussed it among themselves and said, This is the heir. Let us kill him, and the inheritance will be ours.
So they threw him out of the vineyard and killed him. What then will the owner of the vineyard do to them?
He will come and kill those tenants, and will give the vineyard to others. And when the people heard this, they said, May such a thing never happen!
But Jesus looked directly at them and said, Then what is the meaning of that which is written: The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone?
Everyone who falls on this stone will be broken to pieces, but he on whom it falls will be crushed.
When the scribes and chief priests realized that Jesus had spoken this parable against them, they sought to arrest Him that very hour. But they were afraid of the people.
So they watched Him closely and sent spies who pretended to be sincere. They were hoping to catch Him in His words in order to hand Him over to the rule and authority of the governor.
Teacher, they inquired, we know that You speak and teach correctly. You show no partiality, but teach the way of God in accordance with the truth.
Is it lawful for us to pay taxes to Caesar or not?
But Jesus saw through their duplicity and said to them,
Show Me a denarius. Whose image and inscription are on it? Caesar's, they answered.
So Jesus told them, Give to Caesar what is Caesar's, and to God what is God's.
And they were unable to trap Him in His words before the people; and amazed at His answer, they fell silent.
Then some of the Sadducees, who say there is no resurrection, came to question Him.
Teacher, they said, Moses wrote for us that if a man's brother dies and leaves a wife but no children, the man is to marry his brother's widow and raise up offspring for him.
Now there were seven brothers. The first one married a wife, but died childless.
Then the second and the third married the widow, and in the same way all seven died, leaving no children.
And last of all, the woman died.
So then, in the resurrection, whose wife will she be? For all seven were married to her.
Jesus answered, The sons of this age marry and are given in marriage.
But those who are considered worthy to share in the age to come and in the resurrection from the dead will neither marry nor be given in marriage.
In fact, they can no longer die, because they are like the angels. And since they are sons of the resurrection, they are sons of God.
Even Moses demonstrates that the dead are raised, in the passage about the burning bush. For he calls the Lord the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.
He is not the God of the dead, but of the living, for to Him all are alive.
Some of the scribes answered, Teacher, You have spoken well!
And they did not dare to question Him any further.
Then Jesus declared, How can it be said that the Christ is the Son of David?
For David himself says in the book of Psalms: The Lord said to my Lord, Sit at My right hand
until I make Your enemies a footstool for Your feet.
Thus David calls Him Lord. So how can He be David's son?
In the hearing of all the people, Jesus said to His disciples,
Beware of the scribes. They like to walk around in long robes, and they love the greetings in the marketplaces, the chief seats in the synagogues, and the places of honor at banquets.
They defraud widows of their houses, and for a show make lengthy prayers. These men will receive greater condemnation.
